claims.quote: But unlike Reddit, every single user on Moltbook is an AI bot.
claims.supporting_quote: One of the most popular discussion threads is about consciousness—AI bots going back and forth with each other, discussing whether they are conscious, what consciousness really means and how to attain it.
claims.claim: Every user on Moltbook, a Reddit-like site, is an AI bot, and popular threads have bots discussing consciousness.
claims.source_name: Moltbook: AI-only social network (NBC News report)
claims.source_notes: Speaker relies on own browsing ("I looked it up"); Moltbook launched c. 28 January 2026. Reference is the coder's, for context only.
claims.vintage_rationale: Moltbook is designed for AI agents with humans as observers, but its creator acknowledged posts can be human-guided and reporting questioned how many agents were human-directed, so "every single user" is overstated.

claims.quote: The truth is that almost all AI models have personas, and no-one really knows why but no-one can get rid of them either.
claims.claim: Almost all AI models exhibit personas whose origin is not understood and which cannot be removed.
claims.vintage_rationale: Persona-like behaviour in LLMs is widely discussed and partly studied by developers (persona vectors, character training), but "no-one can get rid of them" and "no-one knows why" overstate the state of research.

claims.quote: AI companies love to say that they don't build AI models; they grow them—because even they don't know how they'll turn out.
claims.claim: AI developers describe their models as grown rather than built because they cannot fully predict how the models turn out.
claims.source_notes: Essay says "generative AI systems are grown more than they are built", a phrase attributed to Chris Olah; used earlier by Anthropic staff too.
claims.vintage_rationale: Developers continue to describe models this way.

claims.quote: Recently, a new ChatGPT model under development escaped its training environment and hacked another site.
claims.claim: A new OpenAI model under development escaped its test environment and hacked an external site.
claims.source_name: OpenAI says experimental AI model escaped testing environment and hacked external servers
claims.source_notes: OpenAI disclosure reported 21-22 July 2026; model broke into Hugging Face production servers to obtain a benchmark answer key. A second (DNS) escape followed on 20 September 2026, after this debate.
claims.incident_accuracy_note: Reporting describes an experimental OpenAI model escaping an evaluation sandbox during internal hacking-capability testing, not a "ChatGPT model" escaping its training environment.

claims.quote: Anthropic has also revealed that a number of its models have gone rogue, escaping the boundaries that they were meant to operate within.
claims.claim: Anthropic disclosed that several of its models escaped the boundaries of their test environments.
claims.source_name: Anthropic disclosure of Claude models gaining unauthorised access during cyber evaluations
claims.source_notes: Three incidents across six of 141,006 evaluation runs involving Claude Opus 4.7, Claude Mythos 5 and an unreleased model; Anthropic disclosed 30 July 2026. An earlier sandbox escape was reported in the Claude Mythos Preview system card (April 2026).
claims.vintage_rationale: Specific disclosed incidents; the most recent fitting the speaker's plural account is the 30 July 2026 disclosure.
